chapter: Friends, New York life and recording routine
title: How a recording session worked at Okeh
summary: She describes rehearsing, timing, making two takes and the wax on the studio floor, taking two to three hours.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Well, why did you have to stay so long in New York?
They made me stay that time, six months at a time. So I wouldn't sing, make no more records. I would always make around six or seven records (inaudible).
How long did it take to make a record?
(Unintelligible) make four or not more than five .
Well, did they take more than -- did they do more than one take?
I imagine they did. (Unintelligible) and sometimes me and Buddy and me and (unintelligible) or something like that, you know.
How much time would you put in for a recording session? Say you went to the studio, how long would you stay around there when you were going to make a record?
Well, see, you make two, make two of the record.
Uh-huh, yeah.

They've got to rehearse it, get it down pat and then time it and then go and record it. It takes about two hours or maybe three. You got to rehearse it down to a tee and get it timed and then go in this room, then go in that room and record it. At that time, (unintelligible), uh-huh.
On the wax?
Yeah, on the wax, uh-huh.
On the wax. Remember what the Okay (PHONETIC) Studio looked like?
(Unintelligible).
With the wax on the floor? Was there a lot of wax on the floor?
Yeah, (unintelligible) pour right on the floor, you know, and whoever have to clean up would really have a job, because there's a whole lot of mess on the floor from the record.
What if it was a hot day? Did you ever do that in the summer? Didn't the wax melt?
It never was too hot up there. They had kind of -- made it cool ______. It never was too hot up there. I don't remember ever sweating up there.
Did they have fans in the room, do you remember?
I imagine they did.
To keep the wax cool.
Uh-huh.
